messages:
sanjay: starting canary now for router v3.2.0 + runtime kernel v2.1.4. targeting 10% at first, 20m monitor window. API team: please hold any API-only pins until we confirm KV cache behavior.

deploy-bot: deploy started: router/v3.2.0 -> canary 10% (pods: 3), runtime/v2.1.4 -> canary 2 pods. logs: task queued. :rocket:

lisa: noted. console rollout should stay at 0 until the migration job finishes — the console feature flag depends on the new router routes. can someone sanity-check the migration job?

aj: I ran an infra dry-run earlier. main risk: runtime fast-path toggle causing OOMs under long-context requests. plan: enable fast-path via feature flag after 10m of stable canary metrics. fallback: flip flag off + pin router traffic back to legacy.

maria: tagging SRE: @ops-bot can you keep an eye on 500s and p50/p95 latency for both API and router? set alert if errors >0.5% over 5m.

ops-bot: ack. alert rule applied: "canary-error-rate" => notify eng-sre channel if errors > 0.5% for 5m.

release-bot: canary metrics update (5m): errors 0.12%, p95 latency +3ms, token cost +0.6%. currently green. :white_check_mark:

lisa: good. two asks before we widen: 1) pin API path /v1/generate to v1.5.0 if we see auth header mismatch errors (weird TTL bug). 2) console feature flag stays off until migration job completes.

sanjay: agreed. I'll keep canary at 10% for 20m, then bump to 30% if stable. rollback criteria: errors > 0.8% OR p95 increase > 50ms OR OOM spike on runtime nodes. emergency fallback plan: run this command to re-route all traffic to legacy router and set runtime fast-path off:

```
# fallback to legacy router and disable runtime fast-path
rdeploy traffic shift --service router --to legacy --force
rdeploy feature-toggle --service runtime --flag fast_path --set false
```

aj: noted. also leaving a pin on console routes in the console UI (pin id: pin-2026-03-20-01) so we can quickly revert console exposure.

deploy-bot: canary metrics update (15m): errors 0.18%, p95 +6ms, memory across canary nodes steady. no OOMs.

sanjay: bumping to 30% now. starting 30% window for 15m.

release-bot: 30% window metrics (5m): errors 0.22%, p95 +9ms. traffic distributed: router-canary pods healthy.

maria: migration job still running, ETA ~8m. keeping console flag off.

lisa: quick check — do we have a preflight for quantized model kernels? I want to confirm kernel selection won't regress latency.

aj: yes, perf preflight ran against a 512-token workload. results: quantized kernels +1-3% latency, token cost -18%. will share perf snapshot in #eng-ml after this thread.

ops-bot: alert: canary-error-rate crossed threshold (0.9%) at 1765123602. Notifying eng-sre.

sanjay: seeing the spike, reverting traffic immediately. executing fallback now.

deploy-bot: executing fallback commands...

```
rdeploy traffic shift --service router --to legacy --force
rdeploy feature-toggle --service runtime --flag fast_path --set false
```

release-bot: fallback applied. router traffic = 100% legacy. runtime fast_path = false.

lisa: thanks. starting post-mortem checklist: capture logs from canary nodes, collect flamegraphs if any OOM traces, and capture console migration job timeline.

maria: I'll extend the canary hold and re-run preflight with a larger sample and mem stress. propose next canary after fixes in ~3h.

aj: +1. I'll open a follow-up PR to gate the fast-path behind additional mem checks and add a safer ramp strategy.

sanjay: thanks all. marking this thread for the release notes: note that router v3.2.0 and runtime v2.1.4 attempted canary, snapshot rolled back due to canary error spike; console feature flag was not enabled. Follow-up: fixes + re-run in 3h. :memo:
